title: Boltz-2 Achieves Physics-Grade Drug Binding Affinity Prediction 1,000× Faster
whyItMatters: First open-source AI model to jointly predict 3D biomolecular structure and small-molecule binding affinity near free-energy perturbation (FEP) accuracy at 1,000× speed.
summary: Developed by MIT’s Jameel Clinic and Recursion, Boltz-2 extends open-source biomolecular structure prediction beyond static folding into quantitative thermodynamics. Trained on roughly 5 million binding affinity measurements and molecular dynamics trajectories, it approaches the accuracy of expensive physics-based FEP simulations in ~20 seconds on a single GPU, making high-accuracy virtual screening accessible across academia and biotech.
technicalHighlights: Jointly predicts 3D protein–ligand complex structures and quantitative binding affinity (IC50 / Ki) in a single open-source MIT-licensed model.
Approaches gold-standard physics-based Free Energy Perturbation (FEP) accuracy while running ~1,000× faster.
Demonstrated end-to-end generative hit-finding for diverse, synthesizable small-molecule binders.
caveats: Independent medicinal-chemistry benchmarks note accuracy can still degrade on novel chemical scaffolds far outside training distributions compared with bespoke FEP setups.

scoreRationale.foundational: Bridged the long-standing gap between AI structure prediction and quantitative thermodynamic binding affinity.
scoreRationale.ripple: MIT-licensed open weights drove immediate global adoption across pharmaceutical screening and academic labs.
scoreRationale.verification: Strong bioRxiv benchmarks and CASP16 affinity results, with ongoing independent pharmaceutical evaluations.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed hours of cluster FEP physics simulations into ~18 seconds on a single GPU.
